parole.significato: A type of thin silk fabric, similar to taffeta, characterized by colored stripes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic زَرْدَخَان (zardaḵān) via Andalusian Arabic, of Persian origin.

parole.significato: a member of a powerful faction, native to the Emirate of Granada, and rivals of the abencerrajes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Arabic ثَغْرِيّ (ṯaḡriyy), via Andalusian Arabic, nisba of ثَغْر (ṯaḡr).

Borrowed from Arabic زَجَل (zajal), via Andalusian Arabic.

parole.significato: murderous, homicidal (intending, or likely to commit murder)

parole.significato: used after naranja or naranjo to denote a variety of oranges

parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese mequetrefe, or possibly from Arabic مُخَطْرِف (muḵaṭrif, “raving”).

parole.significato: chemistry (the branch of science concerned with the composition of substances)
parole.testo: From Arabic اَلْكِيمِيَاء (al-kīmiyāʔ), from Ancient Greek χυμείᾱ (khumeíā), or from Latin chimicus, alternative form of chēmicus (“chemical”), from chēmia (“chemistry”), Ancient Greek χυμείᾱ (khumeíā, “art of alloying metals”), from χύμα (khúma, “fluid”).

parole.significato: watermelon (Citrullus lanatus, a vine-like flowering plant)
